opportunities.title: Research Fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be RSC members (Associate Member AMRSC, Member MRSC, or Fellow FRSC) before submitting; hold an independent research post; not currently hold another active Research Fund grant; applications limited to one per department with Head of Department support. Undergraduate Student Members, Affiliates and Partner Scientists are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Supports RSC members with limited access to research funds to start new projects, particularly those in less well-funded institutes, developing countries and early career researchers. Covers chemicals/equipment, consumables, specialist software licences, equipment repairs and equipment access (e.g. synchrotron). Round 1 closed 15 June 2026; Round 2 opens 12 October 2026 and closes 30 November 2026.

opportunities.title: Researcher Collaborations Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants can be PhD students or researchers at any career stage in any sector or location, but must be RSC members (Associate Member AMRSC, Member MRSC, or Fellow FRSC) before submitting and for the grant period. Undergraduate Student Members, Affiliates and Partner Scientists are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Enables researchers to establish and develop collaborations and networks beyond their own institution, including national, international, interdisciplinary and cross-sector collaborations. Funds research visits to potential/current collaborators' institutions and organising meetings/workshops. Round 2 applications opened 3 August 2026 and close 21 September 2026.

opportunities.title: Grants for Carers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be chemists based in the UK or Ireland, or hold valid RSC membership for a minimum of three consecutive years if based outside these countries; must incur additional caring expenses while attending a chemistry-related meeting/conference/workshop or professional development event; must have an active role in the event (except structured training/professional development). Funded by the Chemists' Community Fund.
opportunities.summary: Supports carers to attend a chemistry-related meeting, conference, workshop or professional development event by covering additional costs incurred for care they usually provide (e.g. extra home help/nursing care, respite care, travel for a relative to accompany, extended childminding). Applications are assessed individually, up to £1,200 per year.

opportunities.title: Accessibility Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be chemists based in the UK or Ireland, or hold valid RSC membership for a minimum of three consecutive years if based outside these countries; must use funds to cover support/assistance personally required relating to a disability, impairment or health condition to attend/fully participate in a chemistry-related event; must have an active role in the event (except structured training/professional development). Funded by the Chemists' Community Fund.
opportunities.summary: Supports individuals with disabilities and ongoing health conditions to attend chemistry-related meetings, conferences, workshops or professional development events by covering costs of specific support such as extra travel/accommodation related to accessibility, personal assistance, communication support services, assistive software, and assistive hardware or mobility/sensory aids. Up to £1,200 per year.

opportunities.title: Outreach Fund

amount.raw: Funding amount not stated on page

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be aged 18 and over; be a UK or Republic of Ireland resident (with a UK/ROI address and bank account) or apply on behalf of an organisation registered in the UK/ROI; not resubmit an unsuccessful application unless invited; and have a significant aspect related to the chemical sciences.
opportunities.summary: Funds chemistry-based public engagement and outreach projects that connect communities from all backgrounds with the chemical sciences, including developing chemists' engagement skills, engaging school students and public audiences, and providing under-represented audiences with chemistry engagement opportunities. Open for applications throughout 2026 with rolling deadlines; final deadline 2 October 2026 at 1700 UK time.
